abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, $t(G)$ triangles, and adjacency spectral radius $\lambda(G)>\sqrt m$. Li, Feng and Peng (2025) conjectured that $t(G)\ge\sqrt m-O(1)$ if no vertex belongs to every triangle of $G$. We prove the stronger bound $t(G)\ge\lambda(G)-C$ for an absolute constant $C$, and give an explicit choice of $C$. The proof bounds the sum of the squared adjacency eigenvalues other than the largest and smallest. Interlacing and matrix perturbation estimates then restrict the neighbourhood of a vertex corresponding to a largest entry of a Perron vector to two disjoint edges and isolated vertices. A weighted count of the triangles completes the proof.
hook: Graphs whose triangles share no common vertex have at least about lambda triangles, proving a conjecture
summary: For graphs with spectral radius above the square root of the edge count, the paper shows the triangle count is at least the spectral radius minus a constant, which is stronger than the conjecture of Li, Feng and Peng. The proof bounds eigenvalue sums, uses interlacing and perturbation estimates to pin down the structure near a Perron vector peak, then counts triangles by weights.
title: Triangles without a common vertex
